title: The Provision of the Sepik Basin
premise: Theo Sandoval, a railroad engineer hiding in the Sepik Basin under a dead man's name, has spent six years keeping her map of closed lines out of anyone's hands—lines she helped close after a survey crew's deaths were buried by the company that employed them. When Marcus Vane, the rival who once loved her and betrayed her, hires her crew to reopen those very lines, Theo refuses until he reveals he holds proof of what really happened in the basin: evidence that could clear her brother's name or destroy it. Forced upriver through monsoon season with a leaking boat, a crew she doesn't trust, and Kiri Anselm—a stranger with her own reasons for finding the drowned junction—Theo must decide whether justice outside the law is worth becoming visible again. The story ends at the flooded junction itself, where Theo chooses truth over survival, exposing Vane and the company at the cost of the lines, the map, and the life of invisibility she built.
about_author: Ada Whitlock is a former hydrographic surveyor who spent a decade mapping river systems across Southeast Asia before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people whose work leaves no monuments, drawing on field notebooks she still can't fully explain.

chapters.title: The Weight of Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Theo Sandoval, working under the name Tomas Reyes, surveys a decommissioned spur near the Sepik Basin and burns a page of an old map rather than let it circulate. Her POV establishes her discipline of invisibility and the guilt she carries from a survey accident six years past. Emotional beat: controlled dread beneath routine competence.

chapters.title: A Letter in Wet Ink
chapters.summary: Marcus Vane arrives at Theo's camp with a contract to reopen the closed basin lines—and a photograph proving her brother was alive after the accident the company blamed on him. Theo's POV; she refuses, but the photograph cracks her certainty. Emotional beat: fury colliding with desperate hope.

chapters.title: The Crew That Signs Nothing
chapters.summary: Theo assembles a small crew of men who also live off the books, including boatman Elio Cruz, whose vessel has a hull patch she doesn't trust. Told partly through Elio's POV, we see Theo through others' eyes: competent, cold, afraid of something specific. Emotional beat: uneasy fellowship among the unrecorded.

chapters.title: Terms Written in River Water
chapters.summary: Theo negotiates with Vane: she'll take the job only if the evidence goes to her first, not the company. He agrees too easily, which frightens her more than refusal would have. Her POV; flashback fragments reveal the night of the accident. Emotional beat: suspicion sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Kiri Anselm Boards at Wewak
chapters.summary: At the last supply stop, a stranger forces her way aboard: Kiri Anselm, carrying her father's survey journal—the journal of the man officially blamed for the disaster. Kiri's POV; she believes Theo knows the truth. Emotional beat: two guarded women recognizing each other's lies.

chapters.title: First Water
chapters.summary: The boat enters the basin proper as the monsoon's first rains fall. Elio discovers the hull patch failing faster than expected; rationing begins. Theo's POV, alternating between navigation problems and Kiri's questions she deflects. Emotional beat: the wilderness asserting its indifference.

chapters.title: What the Journal Says
chapters.summary: Kiri reads aloud from her father's journal by lamplight; his final entries describe orders from above to falsify load reports—orders signed by someone whose initials match Vane's. Theo's POV; she says nothing about her own copy of the same orders. Emotional beat: complicity tightening like a rope.

chapters.title: The Crocodile Bank
chapters.summary: Grounding on a silt bank forces the crew overboard in crocodile water; a deckhand is badly injured dragging the boat free. Elio's POV; the crew's loyalty frays, and one man, Sarto, begins asking who hired them and why. Emotional beat: fear turning into mutinous arithmetic.

chapters.title: Vane's Second Letter
chapters.summary: A supply drop includes a message from Vane changing the terms: deliver the reopened line report directly to him, bypassing the company—or the photograph goes to the authorities instead. Theo's POV; she realizes she's being managed, not partnered. Emotional beat: the trap closing quietly.

chapters.title: Night Rain, Open Hands
chapters.summary: Trapped ashore by a storm, Theo finally tells Kiri part of the truth: her brother died trying to expose the falsified reports, and Theo helped close the lines to bury the evidence—including her own signature. Kiri's POV. Emotional beat: confession as relief and new vulnerability; the first tenderness between them.

chapters.title: Sarto's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sarto confronts Theo privately: he's been reporting to Vane since Wewak, and offers to keep silent if she cuts him in on whatever the junction holds. She pretends to agree while planning around him. Theo's POV. Emotional beat: cold clarity; love against duty now has a third claimant—survival.

chapters.title: The Drowned Junction Ahead
chapters.summary: Elio calculates they can reach the old junction in three days if the rain holds off; the hull will not survive the return trip either way. Elio's POV; he tells Theo the boat is a one-way vessel and watches her choose not to turn back. Emotional beat: quiet commitment to a point of no return.

chapters.title: Monsoon Rising
chapters.summary: The storm arrives early. The crew battles a flooded channel at night; the injured deckhand worsens, and Kiri's field medicine keeps him alive. Kiri's POV; she sees Theo lead not from authority but from shared risk. Emotional beat: respect deepening into something neither names.

chapters.title: The Company's Boat
chapters.summary: A company patrol vessel appears upstream—Vane has reported their route, using them as cover for his own arrival. Theo hides the boat in a side channel and realizes Vane intends the junction evidence for himself alone. Theo's POV. Emotional beat: betrayal confirmed; the enemy is inside the mission.

chapters.title: Sarto Jumps Ship
chapters.summary: Sarto deserts toward the patrol boat with the route map, forcing Theo to change course through unmoving swamp to stay ahead. Elio's POV; the crew, now down to four, stops being hired hands and becomes something like comrades. Emotional beat: loss pruning the journey to essentials.

chapters.title: The Leaking Boat and the Long Portage
chapters.summary: With the hull failing, they abandon the boat and portage supplies through flooded forest toward the junction, carrying the injured man on a litter. Kiri's POV; exhaustion strips away pretense, and Theo and Kiri admit what the journey has become between them. Emotional beat: love declared plainly, without promise of tomorrow.

chapters.title: Arrival at the Sepik Junction
chapters.summary: They reach the drowned junction: rusted rails vanishing into black water, and beneath the surface, the wreck of the survey barge—her brother's last workplace. Theo dives and finds the sealed strongbox of original reports. Theo's POV. Emotional beat: grief and vindication surfacing together.

chapters.title: Vane at the Waterline
chapters.summary: Vane arrives with Sarto and armed men, demanding the strongbox; he confesses freely—he ordered the falsification and let her brother die for it, because the truth was worth more buried than told. Theo's POV; she stalls, trading words for time as the river rises. Emotional beat: hatred refined into strategy.

chapters.title: The River Takes Its Evidence
chapters.summary: Theo triggers the demolition charges left on the old trestle, collapsing the junction approach and cutting Vane's men off; in the chaos the strongbox contents are copied and scattered—Kiri carries half, Elio the rest, so no single capture ends it. Kiri's POV. Emotional beat: sacrifice as design; justice distributed beyond any one body.

chapters.title: Outlast the Monsoon
chapters.summary: Stranded by the flood with Vane's party on the far bank, both sides wait out the storm; Theo negotiates via shouted parley, offering Vane exile in exchange for the photograph and his silence. He accepts, broken more by the river than by her. Theo's POV. Emotional beat: victory without triumph; mercy as the harder choice.

chapters.title: Testimony Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Downriver at last, Theo, Kiri, and Elio send the duplicated reports to newspapers, regulators, and the families of the dead crew—bypassing the courts entirely, since the law protected the company for six years. Elio's POV; the injured deckhand survives to carry the story inland. Emotional beat: justice as seed-planting, not verdict.

chapters.title: The Map She Doesn't Burn
chapters.summary: Months later, Theo signs her real name to a public letter reopening the inquiry, then gives Kiri the original map of the closed lines—not burned, but annotated with the truth of every mark. They leave together on a new survey, unhidden. Theo's POV. Emotional beat: visibility chosen freely; memory kept, not buried; love and duty finally pointing the same direction.
